chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Does the man uncover himself when the water is poured, so his private parts are seen, or is the water poured over him, or does he see the private parts of others? He said: My father disliked that from everyone.

key_terms.عَوْرَة: Private parts; that which must be covered
key_terms.يَتَجَرَّدُ: To uncover oneself; to strip naked
key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: To dislike; to find objectionable (in a juristic sense)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on modesty and exposure of private parts while bathing in a public bathhouse?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia emphasis on *haya* (modesty) in communal spaces, tracing the ruling to Imam al-Baqir (AS) to establish a strong prophetic lineage. The Imam’s report that his father 'disliked' (*karaha*) these exposures suggests a recommended precaution (*istihbab*) rather than a strict prohibition, allowing for flexibility in public bathhouses (*hammams*) while maintaining decorum. This reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential approach of balancing social ease with spiritual purity in daily rituals.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can the man be bare during the pouring of the water to see his own private parts, or the water is poured over him, or he see the private parts of the people?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> disliked that from every one’.
en.sarwar: 27. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from more than one person who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Looking at the private parts of non-Muslims is like looking at the private parts of donkeys.’”
